sentences.text: 1 1. Heard Mr. N.J. Dutta, learned counsel for the petitioner Absalom Vankal.

2. The petitioner has filed an application under Section 439 Cr.PC with prayer for bail as he is in jail since 22.10.2022 in connection with Haflong P.S. Case No. 205/2022 (GR Case No. 100/2022)
under Sections 448/363/376(2)(l) IPC.

3. Heard Mr. B.B. Gogoi, learned Addl. P.P. for the State.
4.
I have considered the submissions at the Bar.

Charge Sheet has been laid against the petitioner under Sections 448/363/376(2)(l) IPC.
5.
It is submitted that the petitioner had a love affair with the victim and the statement of the victim as PW-1 clearly reflects that the victim was not assaulted by the petitioner.

It is also submitted that the evidence of the victim's mother as PW-2 clearly reflects that the petitioner is willing to marry the victim but on the contrary the victim's parents have demanded 2 lacs rupees and a pig.
The victim on the other hand is also not willing to get married to the petitioner.
6. I have heard the submissions at the Bar.
It is also submitted at the Bar that the evidence of the witnesses including the victim has already been recorded.
The petitioner has pledged to cooperate with the remaining part of the trial and not to evade the trial.
The petitioner is a local resident.
7. Considering the submissions at the Bar, petition is allowed.

The petitioner shall be enlarged on bail of Rs. 50,000/- with a suitable surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the Sessions Judge,
Dima Hasao, Haflong.
JUDGE
